title: On AI, Trump Should Support Red States
author: Michael Toscano
content:
![On AI, Trump Should Support Red
States](https://www.compactmag.com/content/images/2026/02/Screenshot-2025-08-08-at-4.44.14
---PM-1-1.png)

Late last year, President Trump [_signed an executive
order_](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/12/eliminating-
state-law-obstruction-of-national-artificial-intelligence-
policy/?ref=compactmag.com) aimed at banning states from regulating AI. The
president's constitutional authority unilaterally to block states from passing
laws to protect their citizens from powerful AI systems is [_dubious at
best_](https://law-ai.org/legal-obstacles-to-implementation-of-the-ai-
executive-order/?ref=compactmag.com). But that did nothing to dissuade the
administration's top AI advisor, David Sacks, from forcefully campaigning for
the White House to take this [_uncompromising
path_](https://www.politico.com/news/2025/12/20/big-tech-gets-worried-about-
trumps-ai-czar-00701112?ref=compactmag.com).

Sacks argued that this maneuver was necessary to target blue states like
Colorado for burdening a critical industry with "[_woke
ideology_](https://www.foxbusiness.com/media/white-house-ai-czar-blasts-blue-
states-inserting-woke-ideology-artificial-intelligence?ref=compactmag.com)."
But recent actions by the White House show that this is a canard. The first
major target of this new executive power is not Colorado, California, New
York, or any other blue state. Rather, the president's AI advisors are using
the enormous weight of the executive branch to attack none other than Utah, a
reliably red state, for a bill co-sponsored by two Republican lawmakers.

The bill in question, [_HB
286_](https://le.utah.gov/~2026/bills/static/HB0286.html?ref=compactmag.com),
does not seek to encode a progressive outlook into AI models. It would simply
require AI companies to be transparent about how they test for and protect
against severe risks to children and the public.
